02 · Check the download

A quick check,
before you boot.

A SHA-256 checksum checks that your downloaded image matches the published file. Keep the ISO and SHA256SUMS in the same folder. Open a terminal in that folder and use the command for your system.

Linux
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS

The image should report OK. If it reports a mismatch, download the files again before continuing.

macOS
shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS

The image should report OK.

Windows · PowerShell
Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 .\carpathian-os-development-20261010-r1-x86_64.iso
Get-Content .\SHA256SUMS

Compare the hash returned by the first command with the checksum in the second. Every character must match; uppercase and lowercase letters are equivalent.

03 · A separate place to explore

Give it a fresh
virtual machine.

Use a disposable x86_64 VM with its own new virtual disk. The verified boot path uses legacy BIOS firmware. UEFI boot and a complete installation through to an installed desktop still need qualification.

  1. Create an isolated VM.

    Select Linux and x86_64 in your virtualization software. Choose legacy BIOS firmware for the tested boot path. Allocate resources appropriate to your test environment; measured minimum RAM and storage recommendations are not available yet.

  2. Attach the ISO as a virtual optical disc.

    Use the verified download as the VM’s CD/DVD image and put the optical drive first in its boot order. Keep host disks and shared folders disconnected.

  3. Boot the installer environment.

    The development image has been verified to boot to the BIOS installer environment. Its legacy Carpatic branding is expected. An installation attempt should use only the new disposable virtual disk.

  4. Keep your test separate.

    Full installation, physical hardware, GPU, wireless, Bluetooth, audio and suspend/resume support remain under test. This preview is not ready to replace your everyday operating system.

On an ARM computer?

This image targets x86_64. An ARM host, including Apple Silicon, requires an emulator capable of running that architecture. ARM guest support and host-specific VM instructions are not qualified for this release.
